claims.statement: Treat L1 as a high-variance combat faction whose strength depends on whether objectives, map, and table make its unusually strong invasion and fleet tools relevant.
claims.conditions: Best fit when combat can convert into points or useful leverage; performance may be poor when the game emphasizes economy.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts’ assessment, not tournament data.

claims.statement: Prioritize a high-influence slice, ideally with a blue skip, because tokens sustain repeated activations and a blue skip eases the costly technology path.
claims.conditions: Especially important in six-player and tournament contexts; reconsider L1 if both are absent.
claims.uncertainty: Map-dependent advice; no exact influence threshold is asserted.

claims.statement: Use Diplomacy as a leading round-one option to refresh the five-resource home planet, control timing, and fund technology or production.
claims.conditions: Attractive when the planet is ready to refresh and timing lets you exploit resources twice; consider skips and slice resources.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts rank it highly but call Trade better in some tables.

claims.statement: Consider Leadership when the slice is influence-poor and Diplomacy is likely to remain available for a follow; its tokens help a faction with no home influence.
claims.conditions: Less attractive if Diplomacy is taken before you or Construction rather than Diplomacy is the final pick.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts call Leadership middling and table-order dependent.

claims.statement: Prefer Trade when the table cooperates with debt-meta and commodity washing, since trade goods address L1’s structural economic weakness.
claims.conditions: More valuable with reachable, willing neighbors; without a trade ship, neighbors must come to you, so early cash may trail Diplomacy.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts compare conditional cases and disagree on exact note value.

claims.statement: Do not default to Warfare just to spread farther: the opening already has two-capacity ships, and a concentrated rollout can make L1 a stronger round-three threat.
claims.conditions: Use Warfare when map or objective makes reach more valuable than a stronger fleet build.
claims.uncertainty: Preferred plan, not prohibition.

claims.statement: Technology is the ambitious round-one pick when a double research compensates for awkward starting colors; it has a higher ceiling but depends on economy and follows.
claims.conditions: Choose when funds and Diplomacy or Trade make the secondary affordable.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts call Tech a ceiling play yet describe the opening as expensive.

claims.statement: With no skip, aim toward Gravity Drive, Super Dreadnought II, and Carrier II for flagship movement, dreadnought reach, and capacity for home production.
claims.conditions: A demanding multi-round plan; adapt to tempo and funds.
claims.uncertainty: Recommended path, not required sequence or rules audit.

claims.statement: A blue skip can accelerate Gravity Drive in round one and then be spent on Super Dreadnought II or Carrier II through AI Development Algorithm.
claims.conditions: Exploit the skip repeatedly when research tempo permits.
claims.uncertainty: Exact prerequisite legality was not independently checked.

claims.statement: A yellow skip offers a situational early Cruiser II detour, then can help resume the core dreadnought path.
claims.conditions: Consider when research is affordable and the cruiser has a concrete job.
claims.uncertainty: Modest alternative, not default.

claims.statement: Do not chase Inheritance Systems routinely; the hosts regard its two-yellow path and two-resource activation as too costly.
claims.conditions: Reconsider only with unusual technology tempo or a specific objective.
claims.uncertainty: Strong podcast opinion; current value unverified.

claims.statement: Assimilate makes a planet with an enemy PDS or space dock unusually valuable because the structure becomes an L1 copy before tactical-action production.
claims.conditions: Requires taking such a planet and an opportunity to produce afterward.
claims.uncertainty: Timing is the hosts’ account; full rules legality not reviewed.

claims.statement: Harrow can turn a close ground invasion into a win by applying ships’ bombardment after each ground-combat round.
claims.conditions: Most relevant when bombardment ships are in the active system and the invasion is contested.
claims.uncertainty: Conditional advantage, not automatic win.

claims.statement: Use the starting Super Dreadnought’s two capacity with the carrier to move the opening 2C4I force.
claims.conditions: Account for distance and ground-force needs.
claims.uncertainty: Opening fleet called adequate; expansion depends on slice.

claims.statement: The L1 flagship rewards joining it with dreadnoughts: its hits force assignment to non-fighter ships when possible, pressuring fighter-based fleets.
claims.conditions: Useful for a major battle or to deter attacks in its system.
claims.uncertainty: Fighters still provide hit points and some matchups resist this pressure.

claims.statement: Do not leave mechs in space just to preserve bombardment; once committed to a planet they cannot bombard, and ground-combat sustain is usually more valuable.
claims.conditions: Choose based on whether bombardment or ground presence changes the invasion.
claims.uncertainty: Transcript discusses edge cases; strategic point is clearer than rules details.

claims.statement: The Helmsman can reposition the flagship and dreadnoughts into an empty system, creating a late threat and surprise attack option.
claims.conditions: Destination must lack other players’ ships; opponents can occupy key systems to limit options.
claims.uncertainty: Reflects guide text and 2024 discussion; current rules unchecked.

claims.statement: Project credible force to improve bargaining, but avoid extortion that earns little while damaging future relations.
claims.conditions: Seek equitable point-enabling trades; explain the peaceful deal and preserve mobility for scoring.
claims.uncertainty: Table-dependent political advice.

claims.statement: Avoid a major invasion that only removes a rival if it leaves L1 with an exposed fleet, weak mobility, and no path to score.
claims.conditions: War can be worthwhile for a point, objective, or meaningful leverage.
claims.uncertainty: Common failure pattern, not absolute rule.

claims.statement: Use combat to threaten or execute a decisive late-game winslay while remaining in the scoring pack; the ideal is a strong third- or fourth-place position before that window.
claims.conditions: Needs command tokens, mobility, technology, and fleet to reach relevant systems; do not spend the game stopping others without a scoring plan.
claims.uncertainty: Hosts’ strategic framing; no victory guarantee.

claims.statement: Prepare to pivot into structure objectives by taking opposing structures with Assimilate instead of routinely buying them through Construction.
claims.conditions: May appeal late, even after an opponent scores, when taking a structure advances or blocks an objective.
claims.uncertainty: Control is not guaranteed and aggressive point blocking has political cost.

claims.statement: Combat strength does not itself satisfy control objectives: plan to hold planets, retain command tokens, and meet each objective’s prerequisites.
claims.conditions: Especially important for stage-two or multi-system control objectives.
claims.uncertainty: High-level advice; every objective requirement is not enumerated.

claims.statement: Treat Mecatol Rex plus Imperial as a possible catch-up line, but do not assume taking Mecatol scores a stage one or enables a second status-phase score.
claims.conditions: Requires revealed objectives, qualification, and sufficient tempo; prerequisites and secrets can make it poor.
claims.uncertainty: Not a scoring-rules verification.

claims.statement: Starting Plasma Scoring and bombardment can help with combat secrets such as Turn Their Fleets to Dust or Make an Example of Their World.
claims.conditions: Select only when board state and exact objective timing/conditions align.
claims.uncertainty: Guide notes wording change; do not infer Harrow counts as the bombardment step.

claims.statement: If the game trends toward stage-two tempo, use movement and combat to pursue suitable late control or structure objectives; some single-target objectives may fit L1’s reach.
claims.conditions: Only when mobility, tokens, and actual requirements align; outside-home structure objectives are an exception.
claims.uncertainty: Tendency, not guaranteed scoring.

claims.statement: In Milty-style draft, the guide proposes taking L1 around third or fourth to pursue a high-influence slice, then accepting a later speaker pick that can take Diplomacy.
claims.conditions: Depends on L1 not being an early faction pick and draft availability.
claims.uncertainty: Specific draft advice, not universal map-making advice.

connections.conditions: Harrow applies bombardment after each ground-combat round when the dreadnought is in the active system.
Taking a planet with an enemy space dock can replace it with L1’s dock before tactical-action production.
Flagship and dreadnought hits in its system are assigned to non-fighter ships when able.
Helmsman can move the flagship and dreadnoughts to a system without other players’ ships.
Gravity Drive is prioritized partly for flagship movement and late-game mobility.
The guide treats Super Dreadnought II as a core upgrade for dreadnought reach and combat.
